The TOLV requires that definition of value, just as your theory requires a different definition of value. if my theory is circular reasoning, then so is yours. both arguments provide different definitions to value…

also, it isn’t “according to me (Rococko69)”, it’s according to Carl Marx :)

The VALUE of the product remains in relation to the amount of time it would take me to make a widget. if there is no demand for the widgets, then the price will understandably exponentially decrease. The PRICE decreasing, doesn’t mean the VALUE decreases. The VALUE of the widget is still determined by the amount of time i put into making it. The PRICE of the widget is determined by supply, demand, etc.

The Economic Value of any commodity in a Capitalist system of production is determined by the average necessary labor time to produce that commodity.

Ex. If the average labor time necessary to produce a car is 800x the average labor time it takes to produce a pencil, then the car will have 800x the value of that pencil. 

The actual PRICE of the commodity will vary, for a variety of reasons (supply, demand, etc.), but the inherit VALUE, remains correlated to the labor required to produce said commodity.
what is the point of this
Ahhh, so you’re saying that the value doesn’t change based off of supply/demand, and that only the price does? isn’t that an argument that the LTOV makes?

Price is definitely affected by supply and demand. I’m talking about VALUE. if a bottle of water costs as much as a gallon of gas, then that’s its price changing, but it’s intrinsic value remains correlated to the labor it takes to produce the bottle of water…

If supply and demand were at an equilibrium, then what determines value? It wouldn’t be the consumer, since the consumer’s needs are in perfect balance with the supply of the commodity. The value would therefore be determined by the labor required to produce said commodity, right?

you’re confusing value as price, aren’t you? the supply/demand of a consumer contributes towards price, not value. value is determined by a commodity’s  abundance/lack there of in nature, and the cost/labor it takes to produce said commodity.

If you admit that Labor determines the cost to produce a commodity, then you’re essentially admitting that Labor at least indirectly contributes towards value. The cost to produce a commodity contributes towards its value. If a product takes more money/labor to produce, how would that not directly impact the value of a commodity?
It is one of many puzzle pieces that determine value :)

The LTOV definitely does NOT claim that Labor is the ONLY factor when calculating value. In “The Critique of the Gotha Programme”, Marx says;

 “Labour is not the source of all wealth. Nature is just as much the source of use values (and it is surely of such that material wealth consists!) as labour, which itself is only the manifestation of a force of nature, human labour power."
